A security release: you can reset a forgotten password from the log, every device in a group has a key of its own and a new one waits for approval, an app key seals your secrets, and many routes, paths and sign-in checks are tightened.

**Before you update:** update every instance of a pairing group together, along with the Android app, the browser extension and a relay you run yourself (`knightloader-relay`). Give such a relay the address your devices dial in `KL_RELAY_PUBLIC_URL`, or its names in `KL_RELAY_DOMAIN`, since a device proves who it is only to the relay it means. Every phone, browser and instance then pairs again with the twelve words and waits for approval once. An older app or extension is refused with a message that asks you to update it. A password shorter than 12 characters still signs you in, but the next change needs 12.

## ✨ Added

- **Forgot password? on the sign-in page.** KnightLoader writes a code where only somebody with access to the machine can read it: the container log (on Unraid: Docker tab, KnightLoader icon, Logs), the output of a server started from a terminal or as a service, or `password-reset-code.txt` in the data folder for the desktop app. The code and a new password sign you in, and it is valid for 10 minutes. The reset switches two-factor authentication off, removes every passkey and API token, signs out every other browser and replaces the key sessions are signed with.
- **A reset takes the instance out of its pairing group.** It gets twelve new words that nobody else holds, a relay key entered by hand is removed, and every phone, browser extension and other instance pairs again with the new words. The page after the reset lists what was removed. For 30 days a phone or browser that still holds the old words is told over the relay that the instance was reset and has to be paired again; the old words themselves are not kept.
- **Trusted proxies under Settings, Security.** Behind a reverse proxy, the sign-in limit counts every visitor by the address the proxy reports, so one person guessing at the password no longer makes everybody wait. The relay an instance serves reads the same list. It is empty by default, and the manual says when to fill it in. An entry may cover at most 16 addresses (a /28 for IPv4, a /124 for IPv6), so a whole home network never counts as a proxy; a wider one is kept but marked as not used. The standalone relay takes the list from `KL_RELAY_TRUSTED_PROXIES`.
- **Usenet downloads are checked and repaired with par2.** Once every file of a release is here, KnightLoader checks it against its par2 files and rebuilds the blocks of missing articles, so a release with gaps no longer has to go to a debrid account. Files show Verifying or Repairing in the list, the Android app, Sonarr and Radarr, and nothing is unpacked until the release has passed. A file posted under a random name gets the name its par2 set gives it.
- **Too much damage is caught early.** A release with more damage than its recovery files can rebuild goes to your next account, or fails as soon as that is certain and before the rest of it is downloaded. Only as many recovery files are fetched as the repair needs.
- **KnightLoader opens `.dlc` files itself.** A DLC you upload, drop into a watched folder or get from a site's Click'n'Load button is read on the spot, and its links are staged the way those of an RSDF or CCF are. One that does not open is handed on as before, and the log says why.
- **The extension is on Firefox Add-ons.** The Firefox button in the README and on Settings, Apps opens the listing, with the steps to add and pin it, and the manual names it beside the Chrome and Edge stores.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Five failed sign-ins a minute.** After five wrong passwords or codes from one address within a minute, that address waits until the first of them is a minute old. Before, eight were allowed and the wait was half a minute. IPv6 addresses also share a limit per /48, and at most two password checks run at once, so a flood of guesses cannot tie up the server.
- **A browser whose session has ended returns to the sign-in page** after a reset, a changed password or a sign-out everywhere, instead of showing load errors.
- **The two-factor info mentions the reset.** It says that a password reset from the log switches two-factor authentication off.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A Usenet release whose files finished very quickly could stay in Verifying for good,** and one already known to be lost could fetch its remaining parts anyway. The files of a release now start only after the queue has recorded which files belong to it.
- **An `.nzb` that left out articles finished with a hole.** The file was completed with zeros where the articles belonged and reported as done to Sonarr and Radarr. Those articles now count as missing, so the release goes to your next account or fails with the reason.
- **Progress after a restart was wrong for large Usenet downloads.** A download above about 3 GB that carried on showed no progress, or progress that jumped, and a wrong time left.
- **A forged Usenet article could crash KnightLoader.** An article whose yEnc header named an absurd size, or a server that sent an article or reply line without end, made it reserve far too much memory, and the header could also grow the file on disk. These now count as a damaged article, and the next server is asked for it.
- **A download removed or paused just as it starts stays stopped.** Before, its transfer could keep running and write the whole file with no row in the list, even when you had asked for the files to be deleted. A download paused or removed before it started also stops copying into the temp folder while it waits for further sources or after the skip rule found the file.
- **Restarting or undoing no longer breaks another download.** Restarting a download leaves alone a file that another download with the same name wrote to the same path. Undo after removing a download that is being unpacked keeps it finished, you can paste the link of a finished or failed download brought back with Undo again, and a failed one gets the retry it shows.
- **A paused download whose package was renamed carries on after a restart** where it stopped, in the renamed folder, instead of starting from the first byte.
- **On Windows, a paused live recording stops recording.** Pausing a live yt-dlp recording, renaming its package or removing it without its files left ffmpeg writing into the file, and a Resume started a second recording into the same file. ffmpeg now stops with yt-dlp.
- **Several sources for one file no longer open more connections than a second debrid account allows,** and an account that allows fewer connections for the hoster is no longer asked to unlock the file. Restarting KnightLoader no longer waits for a player paused on the debrid drive.
- **The browser extension no longer fills the Instances page with Browser cards.** It keeps one ID while it is in the group, so a browser in daily use leaves one card, and a browser you remove leaves the group and cannot send links any more.
- **The JDownloader import is more careful.** Packagizer rules whose folder exists only on JDownloader's machine, such as `/output/...` or a Linux path on Windows, arrive unticked with a note. Links rejected by a filter rule or the download history get a line of their own instead of counting as waiting in the link collector.
- **The drop folder only renames what it set aside itself.** A file ending in `.opening` that it had not parked while opening a container keeps its name.
- **Feed entries and the files on a crawled page can no longer point into the local network.** A link that leads further inside the network than the feed or page it came from, such as a LAN or cloud metadata address, is left out and named in the log.
- **Android notifications and permissions behave.** The question about battery optimisation or notifications comes once, even after you flip a switch on the Notifications card. A Captcha waiting notification is removed when you switch every notification off or remove its connection. The QR scanner notices the camera being allowed in Android's settings, and once Android has stopped asking, the button says Open settings.
- **Connect after scanning a pairing code uses the relay from the code** until you type or paste other words, instead of searching the project relay when the instance's own relay was slow to answer.
- **Android: a connection by address whose token was revoked** says it has to be added again with the twelve words, where it showed "unauthorized".
- **The sign-in page says to wait after too many attempts,** where it said "Wrong password." even when the password was right. A refused passkey sign-in says the same.
- **A new password needs at least 12 characters, counted as characters and not bytes,** so a password in another alphabet is held to the same length as one in English. A password over 72 bytes, the most the hash takes, gets its own message on the settings card and the reset form.
- **The extension says "1 file", not "1 files".** The status line on an instance card uses the form each language's plural rules ask for, which matters in languages such as Russian, Polish or Arabic.

## 🔒 Security

- **An app key keeps a copied data folder useless.** Set `KL_APP_KEY` once (make one with `openssl rand -hex 32`) and the password is hashed with Argon2id and peppered with it, while the session key, second factor, recovery codes, stored account keys, passwords and tokens in settings.json and the archive and download passwords are sealed with it. An existing install seals its files at the next start and deletes the unsealed copies after seven days. Without the variable nothing changes, and Settings, Security says how to add one. The desktop apps make their own key.
- **Backups are encrypted with the app key.** A downloaded backup then opens only on an instance with the same key, so keep the key: a restore without it says which key it needs. Backups made before still restore.
- **Every member of a group signs its own calls.** Instances, the Android app and the browser extension each make a key of their own when they join, and every member's id is made from its key, so nobody can sign in another device's name and a device cannot pass itself off as an instance. A call without a signature is refused, and the answers come back signed by the instance that gave them, so a phone or browser only acts on what that instance really said. Calls inside a group no longer carry a token.
- **A new device has to be approved.** A phone, a browser or an instance that enters the twelve words waits under Waiting for approval on the Pairing card, with its kind and key fingerprint, until somebody approves or refuses it. Each device shows its own key (Settings, Pairing on an instance, Settings in the app, the Group card in the extension), so you can check that the waiting card is really the device in your hand before you approve it. The decision reaches every instance of the group. A new instance and the instances already in the group approve each other, so knowing the words is never enough to act as an instance.
- **Removing or refusing a device takes back its key for good.** It can come back only as a new device, which waits for approval again. A removal reaches every instance of the group, and an instance you take out forgets the twelve words. Only an instance with an approved key can make these changes, so a phone or the extension cannot remove anybody.
- **One member cannot crowd out the others.** How many calls wait at once, which request ids are used up, and how many new devices join in an hour are counted per key. A device that waits for approval is never pushed out by newer ones; when an hour has taken in its share, further devices are told to try again later.
- **The phone, the extension and the other instances of a group reach only the routes on a list.** For anything else, the web interface, the Android app and the extension say in your language that you have to sign in on that instance's own web interface. A path that does not exist answers 404.
- **A group member no longer sees secrets or has free rein.** Archive and download passwords, a sign-in or passkey inside a link and a private tracker's passkey are hidden, also for API tokens without the Admin right and on the live stream. A member picks a download folder only inside your download folder or a category's folder, and can remove rows but not erase the files behind them.
- **Another website can no longer change anything through your browser.** A call that changes something and carries a body has to be sent as JSON, and a request your browser marks as started by another site is refused. Scripts that post with `curl -d` need `-H 'Content-Type: application/json'`. Uploads and the doors for Sonarr and Radarr work as before.
- **Without a password, backups, passwords, the twelve words and your files stay put.** Downloading a backup, exporting the settings with their passwords, showing the twelve words again and deleting downloaded files need a login password first. The desktop app's own window still does all four without one.
- **KnightLoader stops taking a domain from a sign-in.** The address it tells its group is only one you typed under Settings, Pairing, Known domains. Domains noted before stay listed until you remove them.
- **Nothing lands in the data folder any more.** A download, unpacking, move or rename that would write next to `auth.json`, `tokens.json` and `settings.json` is refused, however the folder was set or reached. A download folder that contains the data folder is refused too. The built-in `downloads` folder inside it still works, and the row, the rename window and the Android app say why.
- **Logs no longer carry credentials.** Passwords, API keys and tokens in links, feed and indexer addresses and webhook paths are cut from every log line, also in the log you download.
- **A damaged `auth.json` or group file stops the start** instead of loading as empty, which would have dropped the password, every approval and every removal.
- **Clean up removes only what its preview showed.** If the links in a class changed between the preview and your confirmation, nothing is removed and the message says to look again. `POST /api/cleanup/{class}` now takes the `digest` from the preview in a JSON body, with `files` beside it.
- **An older KnightLoader refuses to start on a database a newer one wrote,** as after going back to an older image. It stops with a message that says which version to run.
- **A restored backup brings no passkeys and no database code along.** The passkeys on the running server stay, and triggers and views in an uploaded database are removed.
- **Removing a download with its files no longer deletes another download's file that has a second path.** A symlink, a junction, a bind mount or a different spelling on a disk that ignores case counts as the same file.
- **Signing out ends every copy of the session cookie,** and play links end with the token that asked for them. Revoking a phone's token, changing the password or signing out everywhere ends the play links handed out before, which used to work for up to twelve hours.
- **An authenticator code signs in once.** The same or an older code is refused for the rest of the time it would otherwise be valid.
- **A changed password, a sign-out everywhere and a reset close the live updates** of every open page, and nothing started by a session that ends in the meantime outlasts it. That covers a token, a passkey, a second factor or a pairing group, and a sign-in checked against the old password gets no session. Removing the password also deletes every passkey.
- **Behind a reverse proxy that serves https, the session cookie is marked Secure,** also for the qBittorrent login Sonarr and Radarr use. The relay an instance serves believes `X-Forwarded-For` only from trusted proxies, so a device on the local network cannot dodge the limit on failed handshakes.
- **Limits on what the server reads into memory.** A body sent with an API token stops at 16 MiB, and a finished file asked for through the group is refused rather than loaded whole.
- **Another website could trick you into adding a link.** On an instance without a password, the page the bookmarklet opens refuses to load inside another website, so a hidden button cannot press Add for you.

## 🌐 Translations

- **The motion setting is called Animation** in the web interface and the Android app, in every language.
- **The new sign-in, pairing, approval and refusal messages are in your language** in the web interface, the Android app and the browser extension.
